Pharmacology Department Celebrates 5th Pharmacovigilance Week
Friday, 26 September 2025
1552 Hits
The Department of Pharmacology, Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences, Sevagram, in collaboration with the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI), celebrated the 5th National Pharmacovigilance Week from 17th to 23rd September 2025. The week was observed with the theme “Your Safety, Just a Click Away—Report to PvPI”, highlighting the importance of adverse drug reaction (ADR) reporting and building a culture of patient safety.
The week-long programme featured sensitization sessions, guest lectures, academic training, and creative events that engaged MBBS students, postgraduates, nursing students, and faculty. Dr. Snehalata Gajbhiye from AIIMS delivered a guest lecture, underscoring the crucial role of pharmacovigilance in everyday clinical practice. Sessions also covered ADR identification, materiovigilance, causality assessment, and adaptive clinical trial designs.
To blend creativity with awareness, poster, painting, and sketch competitions were organized, along with interactive quizzes for medical students. These activities not only spread awareness but also inspired young healthcare professionals to take active roles in ADR reporting and safe medication practices.
The celebrations concluded with a valedictory session, certificate distribution, and reflections by faculty members. The Department of Pharmacology—led by Professor & Head Dr. Devesh Gosavi, along with faculty members Dr. Ranjana Kale, Dr. Leena Chimurkar, Dr. Mohan Pethe, postgraduate students, PvPI Associate Mr. Swamy Bandi, and interns—emphasized their ongoing commitment to fostering a vigilant healthcare environment.
"The observance of Pharmacovigilance Week at MGIMS served as a strong reminder of the need for collaborative, innovative, and sustained efforts to ensure patient safety. It will also promote pharmacovigilance practices that inspire future generations of healthcare providers", said Dr Dr. Devesh Gosavi (Head of Department of Pharmacology, MGIMS)
